Noon overhead through a gap in the canopy, the stream bed burning amber-gold straight through clear water, hulls sailing over their own crisp black shadows on the gravel, a dragonfly's shadow keeping perfect pace beside them and losing only at the bend.

Late sun angled down the full length of the channel, turning the surface to hammered copper while both banks sink into cool ink-blue, every hull's wake shattering the copper into hundreds of bright scattered flecks, a snail on the bank overtaking the third-place boat.

A moving net of ripple-light thrown restlessly up onto the undersides of the overhanging roots, honey-gold against deep cool jade, the water below it a shifting dark emerald, and one root wearing a single bright fleck like a wandering eye.

Early morning, the sun still low and rosy, its soft glow skimming the surface and catching every ripple-crest in rose-gold while the water between crests holds a deep turquoise, a seed-pod bailed out mid-race with a cupped acorn scooping the bilge.

A soft shaft dropping through a single gap in the canopy onto one patch of water in mid-channel, blazing pearl-white there while all around it the stream runs in deep cool jade shade, motes turning slowly inside the bright pool.

Evening, the sky still scarlet above the treeline, the water holding it in long broken streaks of scarlet and lilac, the first fireflies doubled on the surface, each a trembling point of amber against the cool shadow between the streaks.

Full overcast breaking apart at the horizon so a flat silver glow floods low across the surface, the water shifting between cool pewter and saturated jade, the wet moss on the bank burning an almost violent green in the diffuse bright light.

Midsummer midday, sun punching straight through thin canopy, the stream bed a continuous sheet of warm gold visible through clear water, hulls casting hard ink shadows on the pale gravel beneath, a beetle gripping a thwart as its shadow races beside it.

The last direct sun catching spray thrown up by the lead hull, the droplets hanging as a bright copper dust backlit against the cool blue-green shadow of the far bank, a mouse in a walnut-shell riding the wake, also catching the light.

A mirror-still pool where the channel briefly widens before the rapids, the whole fleet doubled in it perfectly, amber hulls and scarlet sails reflected without distortion, a water-strider crossing the reflection of a sail and bending it into a curved smear of rose.

Dusk, rose still holding in the sky, the long water below it turning the same rose broken by cool lilac in the shadows of the banks, the berry-lanterns hung low enough that each has its own trembling doubled glow on the surface.

Mid-morning, sunlight fracturing through wind-shaken canopy into a restless dappling across the whole surface, patches of warm gold leaping and vanishing on the turquoise water, a dandelion seed rigged as a spare sail lit bright gold each time a patch finds it.

The sun exactly level with the water at low evening, its full glow streaking the entire surface in beaten amber, every ripple a bright fleck while the wake-troughs hold cool ink-blue, the near bank already in full blue shadow.

Reflected ripple-light moving in a slow restless net across the underside of a low stone bridge the fleet passes under, honey-amber against the cool jade of the stone, the racers briefly gilded and then released back into open shade.

A heavy afternoon haze thinning at one point above the channel, letting a soft wide pool of pearl-white light lie on the surface there, the water under it a pale luminous emerald, the rest of the channel a deep cool turquoise by contrast.

Thin bright rain beginning, every drop ringed in a small perfect circle of light on the pewter surface, the wet canopy above dripping secondary drops, the bank moss a saturated jade against the silver-grey glow, a boat's marigold sail darkening with wet.

Full midday striking a straight reach, the stream bed alternating pale sand and dark weed, lit gold and jade straight through the clear water, the hulls throwing paired shadows, one sharp on sand, one swallowed in the weed's dark green.

Sunrise, the first direct light still cool rose and hitting the surface at a flat angle so every ripple-crest glows rose while its shadow side is a deep lilac, a copper-hulled boat skimming the bright crests and disappearing into shadow between them.

Evening fireflies beginning before the sky is fully dark, rose still overhead, each firefly and each hung lantern-berry doubled on the still water as a paired amber point, the surface between them a deep turquoise holding the last of the sky.

Spray arcing off a rock mid-channel, the low sun catching it from behind so it hangs as a bright amber dust in the air, the shadow behind the rock a deep cool emerald pool where the water runs slack and dark.

Late afternoon, the canopy casting deep jade shade across most of the surface with one bright gap throwing a soft shaft of gold onto a single mid-channel patch, the water there luminous, a boot-shaped seed-pod floating through it briefly blazing.

The surface in full shade except where the far bank dips and lets in a long low streak of amber afternoon light across the water, the streak alive with bright flecks from passing wakes, the rest of the channel a cool dark jade.

Midday overhead, the water so clear the stream bed's copper and rose quartz gravel is fully visible below the jade water, every hull's shadow a crisp shape on the bottom, a water-snail leaving its own thin shadow-trail on the pale gravel.

Storm light, the sky a saturated jade-green before rain, one gap letting a raw gold glow fall in a wide soft pool on the surface, the colour contrast between the gold pool and the surrounding green so strong it reads as unreal.

Evening mist lying low and thin over the water, the surface visible through it as a dark turquoise glowing faintly through the white, berry-lanterns casting amber pools that spread and soften in the mist, doubling as smeared warm glow on the water below.
